correctness.rationale: PASS. Reconstructed lambda_S(p^a)=1 if p in S and 1+lambda_S(a) otherwise; for a composite, take the minimum across prime-power factors. Induction gives the unique least depth-i witness M_1=q, M_{i+1}=r^{M_i}. For large i, every other depth-i exponent is >=2M_i (different base s>r, increased exponent or extra factor); depth>i starts at least M_{i+1}. The Euler product is legitimate: tail obstructions at primes p>P have total density <=sum_{p>P}p^{-q}, while finite-prime large-exponent tails are summable. Hence delta_infinity=product B_{S,p}>0. Conditioning on v_r(n)=M_i with all other valuations fully avoiding yields leading density K_S*r^{-M_i}; additional valuations at r are O(r^{-2M_i}) and those at p>=s are O(s^{-M_i}). Identical squeezing gives delta_i-delta_{i+1}. Independent SPF mosaic recursion checked q={2,3} and S={2,3} small witnesses, but finite checks are not the infinite proof.
